develop the approved project from an initial

lessons.title: **Capstone Orientation** — Explain why one learner-owned project develops throughout the course and how evaluation differs from optional practice.
**Users and Problems** — Identify a specific user, useful task, and observable improvement.
**CLI Contracts** — Define commands, input formats, output behavior, exit codes, and safe file effects.
**Acceptance Scenarios** — Specify normal, empty, boundary, invalid, and failure cases with checkable expected behavior.
**Scope and Risk** — Distinguish achievable core work from optional stretch features and identify environmental constraints.
**Scope Review** — Evaluate feasibility and record an explicit approval or structured self-review before substantial implementation.
**System Decomposition** — Separate parsing, validation, core processing, and reporting into justified components.
**Interfaces and Ownership** — Describe data movement, errors, resource ownership, and trust boundaries.
**Data Structures** — Select a useful representation and explain the alternatives.
**Algorithmic Reasoning** — Estimate correctness constraints, time cost, and space cost under stated assumptions.
**Test Strategy** — Map acceptance cases and risks to initial tests and fixtures.
**Design Review** — Challenge an architectural assumption and record the response and first vertical slice.
**Project Setup** — Establish a version-controlled project and documented build/test commands.
**First Failing Test** — Define an acceptance test that exposes missing behavior before implementing it.
**Vertical Slice** — Implement one useful command-to-result path with all relevant layers connected.
**Input Validation** — Handle malformed, empty, and boundary inputs safely.
**Debugging and Regression** — Reproduce a failure, correct it, and retain a test preventing recurrence.
**Versioned Iteration** — Evolve the same project through explainable commits and repeatable checks.
**Measurement Design** — Choose a meaningful property, fixed fixtures, units, and relevant environment conditions.
**Baseline Analysis** — Collect repeated measurements and describe variability and limitations.
**Evidence-Based Revision** — Make or reject a justified change using comparable before/after results.
**Technical Documentation** — Write clear setup, use, testing, failure-handling, and architecture instructions.
**Reproducible Packaging** — Prepare a build or release that does not depend on undocumented local state.
**Release Verification** — Repeat declared test/build/package checks from a clean checkout.
**Requirements Traceability** — Link each mandatory acceptance case to code, tests, observations, or explanation.
**Failure-Path Review** — Check cleanup, permissions, invalid data, and critical safety conditions.
**Clean-Start Reproduction** — Rebuild and rerun the project without relying on the original working directory.
**Evidence Review** — Compare actual implementation and measurements with the submitted claims.
**Finding Remediation** — Correct material defects and retain regression evidence.
**Defense Preparation** — Organize a reviewer-accessible explanation without supplying scripted answers.
**Release Inspection** — Present the approved scope, delivered behavior, tests, version history, and reproducible build.
**Design Defense** — Explain actual algorithm and data choices, interfaces, errors, and limitations.
**Measurement Defense** — Interpret what the evidence proves and what remains uncertain.
**Independent Change** — Diagnose a bounded new case or implement a small change without an assistant.
**Final Evaluation** — Apply the published rubric and record pass or specific revise-and-reassess findings.

outcomes.description: Select and bound a useful developer-utility problem with users, safe operating constraints, testable acceptance cases, and explicit exclusions.
Design a modular architecture with clear interfaces and justify at least one substantial data-structure and algorithmic choice, including time/space reasoning.
Implement a usable, safe CLI incrementally with meaningful version history, input contracts, error handling, and reproducible behavior.
Use automated tests, debugging, and a repeatable CI or equivalent local workflow to verify normal, boundary, invalid, and operational-failure cases.
Measure a meaningful engineering property under controlled conditions and use a documented before/after comparison to justify a technical decision.
Package and document the project for clean-checkout installation, execution, testing, and independent evaluation.
Relate each core requirement to inspectable evidence, reproduce the project independently, and resolve material review and safety findings.
Defend the implementation, limitations, trade-offs, and any AI assistance, and complete a scoped change or debugging challenge without an assistant.
